purpose: Replace the break-even projection's assumed fixed-cost share with a measured per-segment breakdown on the TP1 arm, and record the host-side term the projection omits.

protocol.note: the harness reads back every token, so its window per step includes a sampler readback the tok/s protocol amortizes; kernel-family times are device time and are unaffected

findings: Attention, GDN, sampler and copy kernels together are 1.578 ms/step on the W7900 and 1.441 ms/step on the XTX. That is 4.7% and 5.1% of each card's own TP1 token time, and 5.6% / 5.1% of the faster arm's token time that the projection actually compares against. Even adding every unnamed kernel in the 'other' family (norms, rope, residual, setup) only reaches 11.9% and 12.9% of each card's own token time. The projection's 20% and 30% rows therefore sit above anything these measurements support; the 0-10% rows are the defensible range, and the exchange's projection is inside budget there too.

The weight-read kernels are 25.95 ms/step (W7900) and 21.77 ms/step (XTX) - 77% and 77% of each card's own token time - and their 1.19x ratio matches the two cards' bandwidth ratio and their 1.20x TP1 token-rate ratio. Sharding the weight read is where the compute saving is, and it is also why the fixed share is small.

Each decode step issues ~811 kernel launches. That is the number that decides whether a sharded rank can stay inside its budget, because launch points are per rank and the group waits for the slower rank.

The harness's window also contains a per-token sampler readback (about 9 ms/step of hipMemcpy API time) that the tok/s protocol amortizes, so its interior-gap split is not the tok/s protocol's. It is recorded as a candidate missing term rather than as the projection's host cost: 19.2 ms (W7900) and 22.2 ms (XTX) of interior gap per step, of which 15.3 and 16.2 ms has no HIP API in flight. A trace of the tok/s protocol itself, or an in-engine launch-gap counter, is what would settle it.

sources.w7900: rocprofv3 kernel/marker/HIP/memory-copy trace of the R0 resident session, 512 prompt rows, 128 decode tokens, HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

limitations: Kernel-family attribution is device time from a rocprofv3 trace of the R0 resident session. It is not a shard-shaped segment measurement: no shard-shaped weight layout exists in the engine, so the sharded MLP/attention/GDN segment times the decision rule needs are still unmeasured.

The interior-gap split is specific to this harness, which reads back every token; the tok/s protocol amortizes that readback. Gap numbers are indicative of the launch structure, not exact for the tok/s protocol.
No compute -> exchange -> compute sequence has been measured.
Both cards are gfx1100 and were measured in the same session with the same protocol, so the two columns are comparable to each other.
next_measurements: A shard-shaped MLP segment: build a half-intermediate Q4_K weight layout and time the engine's own GEMV dispatch on it, on both cards, so the compute saving is measured rather than assumed.
Replicated versus single-owner attention and GDN segment times at full and half head counts.
Representative compute -> exchange -> compute sequences using the native transport, at the measured per-reduction cost.
A launch-gap measurement on the tok/s protocol path, so the projection's omitted host term is bounded.
